title: Static projection publishing: the Markus site as a projection of the content
description:
# Static projection publishing: the Markus site as a projection of the content

## Vision (Ryan)
The default publication option for Markus sites is static files in a versioned S3 bucket behind our own CloudFront. The published site is a projection of the content through Markus, not "a build we trigger". The common update is a single-item edit, rendered incrementally and immediately by a Lambda in the GraphQL API path (the existing content-actions custom mutation), writing only the pages that depend on that item. No CodeBuild, no Amplify reader app, no prominent republish button; a full re-projection is an ops maintenance command, like rebuilding a database index. The same GraphQL API's public surface can serve dynamic features on the static pages. Later, an extension/plugin protocol, extracted from a first real plugin.

Design: /Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md (v1, superseded direction: markus-publication-architecture.md).

## Measured facts behind it (2026-10-12, see v2 section 1)
- Markus in-process: 2 ms median per page; whole Anth.us site in-process from warm caches is byte-identical (2,352 files) to today's build.
- Cold Anth.us build 283 s locally, 236 s of it image encoding; warm 54 s, 28 s of it one markus subprocess per page.
- content-actions is already a Python 3.12 arm64 zip Lambda (18.5 MB) bundling Markus 0.5.1, Pillow, citeproc; Init 260-345 ms; today's publish takes 1.9-2.8 s (AppSync round trips).

## Decisions already made / constraints
- No CodeBuild, no build job, no Amplify reader app for Markus sites.
- Default publication option for Markus sites = S3 projection (`publication.kind = "s3-projection"`).
- Pre-production sites (Pilobol.us) move fast; Anth.us (production) gets downtime care, parity gates and Ryan's yes per production step.
- Per-site Google projects (unchanged).
- Ryan retires old resources himself (reader apps, buckets, stacks).
- No email addresses in repos (placeholders in specs; allowlists in AWS config).
- Kanbus only through kbs; never edit project/ files by hand.

## Milestones (epics, in dependency order)
M0 spike, M1 projection core + template option, M2 renditions at upload, M3 incremental dependents + reconcile, M4 cache strategy, M5 Pilobol.us migration, M6 Anth.us migration, M7 retire reader apps + template cleanup, M8 public surface, M9 first plugin -> extension protocol, M10 docs + README diagram.

Related (not children): PPY-1f1489 (four-site alignment), PPY-7d8cd0 (Phase 6 moves).
right_now_summary: M1 is merged and released, while rollout checks and later migration work are still pending.
